_notes: 2026-11-18, the user's cliff-edge picture ('can we achieve something closer to this?'): Rim Ledge, flat-topped slabs of layered grey stone that form a cliff's lip and jut out over the drop, lichen on the top only. Nordic stone, not the photo's sandstone; the photo is licensed stock and never an input.
World props the user asked for (2026-11-13): interesting, unique things to place around the world, 'for example magical stones with blue, glowing runes'.

Made like the gathering nodes: concept image, Hunyuan3D shape + UltraTex texture, Tools/Blender/ingest_generated.py (atlas, LODs, collider, height/moss masks, glow), then AgentScripts/BuildWorldProps.cs.
Run: D:\ComfyUI\.venv\Scripts\python.exe Tools/LocalSpawn/generate_gathering.py --group props [images|3d|ingest|all] [asset ...] (Unity closed for 3d).
width: metres across the widest side in the game; max_height caps a tall look. glow: emission from the albedo ('hue' near a colour), tinted.
The runes are painted pale blue and matte in the concept (a glowing concept makes UltraTex paint flat colour); the game makes them glow from the emission map.
UltraTex (FLUX) is a non-commercial licence and Hunyuan3D's licence excludes some territories: re-texture/check before a release.
2026-11-14: the raids' and items' primitive stand-ins (Cache Crate to Shaman Staff); built into their prefabs by BuildStructureModels.Placeholders, not BuildWorldProps.

common: Three-quarter view from slightly above, whole object visible and centred, isolated on a plain light grey background. Matte, softly lit, no glow, no light rays, no fog.

looks.prompt: A single tall Viking age rune stone standing upright in the ground: one slab of pale grey granite, about two and a half metres tall and a metre wide, weathered and slightly leaning, its edges rounded by centuries, patches of grey-green lichen near the base. A long band of Norse runes carved deep into its face follows the edge in a curving serpent-shaped ribbon, and a simple knot carving in the middle; the carved grooves of the runes are filled with bright pale blue paint that stands out clearly against the grey stone. One solid stone, nothing loose.

A single old wayside cairn from Norse folklore: a waist-high rounded pile of flat grey field stones stacked tightly into one solid mound, a little moss in the gaps, and on its top one upright flat stone carved with three large Norse runes whose grooves are filled with bright pale blue paint, clearly visible. Everything grown into one solid piece, nothing loose or floating.

A single low Norse offering stone in a forest clearing: a broad, flat-topped grey boulder about knee high, its top worn smooth, with a round bowl hollowed into it holding a little dark water, a few carved spiral lines around the bowl, and on the top beside the bowl a small offering of a deer antler and a handful of red berries, all lying flat and grown into the stone. Moss on the shaded side. One solid object.

A single old Norse wooden idol post standing in the ground: one thick weathered tree trunk about two metres tall, grey and cracked with age, carved at the top into a stern bearded face with deep-set eyes and a pointed helmet, the carving softened by rain, and below the face a few bands of carved knotwork; strips of faded red cloth tied around its middle. One solid object, nothing floating.

A single large mossy grey boulder in a Nordic forest that looks just like a huge troll curled up asleep and turned to stone: a hunched rounded back, a big lumpy head resting on its folded arms with a long drooping nose and closed heavy eyelids, a few stone knuckles at the front, thick green moss and small ferns on the back like hair. Clearly a rock, but you can see the sleeping troll in it. One solid stone.
An old weathered wooden supply crate without its lid, open at the top and empty inside, thick grey planks, black iron corner bands and a rope handle on each end.

A single loose wooden lid for a crate, lying flat on the floor and seen from above at an angle: four grey weathered planks side by side, thin like a board, held together by two black iron straps across them. Nothing under it.
A round flat platform of old fitted grey flagstones about three metres across, worn smooth, a ring of carved runes around its edge, moss in the joints. Matte.
A tall narrow weathered waystone: a flat-sided grey standing stone with a carved rune circle on its face and short lines of pale blue runes below it, lichen on its top. Matte runes.

The burned-out ruin of a small old Norse longhouse seen from the side: two rows of charred black wall posts of different heights, two blackened roof beams still lying across them, two fallen beams leaning on the ground, a tall ruined chimney of soot-blackened field stones at one end, ash and charcoal on the ground. No fire, no smoke.

A collapsing old Norse wooden watchtower: four tall grey weathered log posts, one of them broken shorter, a sagging broken plank platform at the top, loose diagonal braces, and one post fallen on the ground beside it.
One long old weathered bone, the leg bone of a large animal, grey-white and cracked.
A tall thin stranger standing still in a long tattered grey wool cloak and deep hood, the face hidden in shadow, both hands resting on a gnarled walking staff.
A plain narrow weathered grey standing stone, lichen-spotted, leaning a little.
A Viking age hand torch: a short rough wooden stick, its top end thickly wrapped in dark brown tarred rags bound round with twine. Unlit: no flame, no smoke, no metal.
A simple wooden fishing rod: a long thin tapering hazel pole with a small wooden line reel near the handle.
A gnarled twisted wooden staff with a forked top, moss and tiny mushrooms growing along it.

An old Norse stone bridge over a mountain river: a single round arch of rough grey granite blocks laid without mortar, about fourteen metres long and three metres wide, a flat cobbled deck, low uneven parapet walls of stacked stones along both sides, heavy stone abutments at both ends, moss and grey-green lichen in the joints, the deck stones worn smooth down the middle, two old iron rings set into one parapet. Seen from the side and a little above, the whole bridge visible, no water and no ground under it.

A ruined, long-abandoned mountain summer farm hut (a Norwegian seter): a small log cabin of dark grey weathered timber on a low dry-stone foundation, half of its roof fallen in so the rafters and the dark inside show, the remaining roof covered in a smooth layer of bare dark brown peat earth over birch bark, no grass, no straw, nothing shaggy, the door hanging off one hinge, the top logs of one wall tumbled, a broken wooden milk churn and a fallen fence rail beside it.

edit.instruction: Make this an abandoned ruin: let the left half of the roof collapse into the hut so the bare rafters and the dark inside show, tumble the top logs of the front wall, and make the remaining roof a smooth layer of bare dark brown peat earth with no grass, straw or shaggy fibres. Keep the same hut, timber, stone foundation, milk churn, fence, viewing angle, size and plain light grey background.

looks.prompt: A troll's heap of gnawed bones in a low mound: cattle and sheep skulls, broken ribs, cracked thigh bones and a few old antlers piled together, brown and grey with age, some split open for the marrow, on a patch of bare flat rock.

A troll's hoard heaped on a flat rock: tarnished dark silver coins and twisted arm rings in a low pile, a dented iron-bound wooden chest with its lid open, two old rusted swords and an axe head, a cracked drinking horn and a dull bronze bowl, all darkened and dull with age, nothing shining.

A troll turned to stone by the dawn in the middle of a stride, in the manner of Theodor Kittelsen's and John Bauer's Norwegian trolls, not an ape, not a gorilla, no fur on the body: a small head on huge hunched shoulders, a long drooping hooked nose, huge sticking-out ears, tiny deep-set eyes, a wide lipless mouth with two blunt tusks, lumpy hairless skin as grey and rough as weathered granite: now one weathered grey granite rock, one foot forward in a long stride, one long arm raised across its face against the sunrise, the other hanging to its knee, its nose and ears still clear but worn round, deep cracks through the stone, patches of grey-green moss and orange lichen, on a broken rocky base. All one piece of stone.

A huge crude troll club: a heavy pine trunk, thin and rubbed smooth at the grip end and swelling to a massive knotted head studded with stumps of broken branches, a wide rusted iron band from an old bridge hammered round the head, dark with old stains. Lying flat on its side.

edit.instruction: Make this into a long troll club lying on its side: stretch it into a long tapering pine trunk about three times as long, thin and rubbed smooth at the grip end, swelling to the massive knotted head with the broken branch stumps and the rusted iron band. Keep the same wood, iron band, lighting and plain light grey background.

looks.prompt: A small drying stack of hand-cut peat on a bog: irregular soft-edged sods of black-brown peat, fibrous and crumbly with roots showing, leaned against each other in a loose little stack about knee high with gaps for the wind, some sods fallen at the foot, on a patch of wet brown ground.

The weathered ruin of a crude Viking age bloomery for smelting bog iron, centuries old: a low lumpy shaft furnace of rough hand-built clay and fieldstones, knee to waist high, its top broken off and one side collapsed, the clay cracked and baked in uneven red-brown and grey patches, soot-black inside, half sunk in the ground, a low heap of dark lumpy slag beside it and a few rusty brown lumps of bog ore. Ancient and earthy, nothing smooth or modern.

One straight section of an old boardwalk across a bog, four metres long and one metre wide: weathered grey wooden planks laid across two split-log stringers resting on short wooden posts, the plank ends uneven, one plank cracked and one missing, a little green moss on the wood. Both ends cut off square, nothing else around it.

A small old Norse rowboat (a faering): a light clinker-built hull of overlapping dark tarred oak planks with iron rivets, a raised curved stem and stern, two thwarts across it, wooden tholepins for the oars, worn and weathered, empty. Seen from the side and a little above, the whole boat visible, no water.

An old Hardanger fiddle drowned in a bog for a hundred years: blackened and warped dark wood, the carved scroll head shaped like a horse's head, broken strings curling loose, pale water stains and a few strands of black pondweed caught in the pegs, the mother-of-pearl inlay dull. Lying flat.

A single old farm boundary stone: a rough grey granite post about a metre tall, roughly squared, with a simple cross cut into its top and a few worn notches on its face, moss on one side and at its foot.

A square, perfectly flat and level platform of old grey cobblestones laid on a thick slab of rough stacked granite blocks about a metre thick, the platform about eight metres wide and eight metres long, a low wall of stacked rough grey stone blocks along two opposite edges, the other two edges open and cut square and rough as if broken off, moss and grey-green lichen in the joints. Seen at a three-quarter angle from above. Flat box shape, no arch, no curve, no hump, no steps, no ramp.

A massive square bridge pier standing alone, built of many rough uneven grey granite blocks of different sizes laid without mortar, deep dark joints between them, about four metres square at the top and wider at its foot, about fourteen metres tall, a flat level top of large slabs, dark wet stains and green moss near the foot, grey-green lichen higher up. Rough, old and hand-built, not smooth. Nothing on top of it, no bridge, no ground and no water.

A troll's toll pole: one single crooked upright pole of dark weathered wood about two and a half metres tall with a forked top, a big horned animal skull fixed in the fork, strings of old copper coins on leather thongs and a few long bones lashed to the pole with rope, a small flat offering stone at its foot with a few coins on it. No crossbar, no sign, nothing else.

A single huge slab of weathered grey Nordic granite that forms the very edge of a cliff, seen as one loose piece: a broad, almost level flat top with crusty patches of ochre-yellow and pale grey-green lichen on the top surface only, the front face made of three horizontal stacked beds of rock of different thickness, the top bed jutting forward as an overhanging lip with a dark worn hollow underneath it, a few straight vertical cracks running down through the beds. Hard, angular, solid rock with fine grain, no pebbles, no grass, no moss carpet, no tree, no soil. One solid stone.

A single huge slab of weathered grey Nordic granite that forms the very edge of a cliff, seen as one loose piece: a broad, almost level flat top with crusty patches of ochre-yellow and pale grey-green lichen on the top surface only, the front face made of four horizontal stacked beds of rock of different thickness, the top bed jutting forward as an overhanging lip with a dark worn hollow underneath it, split into two big blocks by one deep crack, the left block a little lower, and a small broken corner at one end. Hard, angular, solid rock with fine grain, no pebbles, no grass, no moss carpet, no tree, no soil. One solid stone.

A single huge slab of weathered grey Nordic granite that forms the very edge of a cliff, seen as one loose piece: a broad, almost level flat top with crusty patches of ochre-yellow and pale grey-green lichen on the top surface only, the front face made of two thick horizontal stacked beds of rock of different thickness, the top bed jutting forward as an overhanging lip with a dark worn hollow underneath it, long and low, the lip overhanging far at the middle, the ends worn rounder. Hard, angular, solid rock with fine grain, no pebbles, no grass, no moss carpet, no tree, no soil. One solid stone.

A rough Norse hunters' lean-to shelter in the forest: three slanted wooden poles lashed to a crossbar, stretched stitched brown animal hides pulled over them and tied down with rope, open at the front, a rolled fur bedroll and a wooden bowl inside on the ground, a few stones holding down the hide edges. Everything grown together into one solid piece, nothing loose or floating.

A rough Norse camp drying rack: a frame of grey weathered branches lashed together with rope, strips of dark dried meat and a stretched grey wolf pelt hanging from the top pole, a few bones at its foot. Everything grown together into one solid piece, nothing loose or floating.

A raiders' stash of plunder: a bulging bundle of goods wrapped tight in a stitched brown hide and tied with thick rope, sitting on a few flat grey stones, a small iron-bound wooden box and a dented copper pot tucked against it, an antler tied to the top. Everything grown together into one solid piece, nothing loose or floating.

A fresh rockslide: a low fan-shaped heap of sharp, newly broken pale grey rocks of many sizes spilled across the ground, and sticking out from under the rocks a crushed wooden pack frame with a torn sack and the broken handle of a pickaxe. Everything grown together into one solid piece, nothing loose or floating.

A huge soot-blackened iron cauldron from Norse folklore, big enough to sit a man in, standing on three rough grey boulders over a heap of charred logs and grey ash, thick grey stew inside with large bones and a cow's skull sticking out over the rim, a giant crude wooden ladle leaning against it. Everything grown together into one solid piece, nothing loose or floating.

A weathered grey wooden fence post with a long straight Norwegian lur herding horn hanging from it on a leather strap: the horn is about a metre and a half long, slender, made of wood wound tightly in pale birch bark, flaring at the end; at the foot of the post a short stretch of old dry-stone wall with moss on top. Everything grown together into one solid piece, nothing loose or floating.

A preserved bog body like those found in Scandinavian peat bogs, as seen in a museum, not gory: a small curled human figure with dark brown leathery skin lying half sunk in black wet peat and green sphagnum moss, wrapped in rotten dark wool rags, one hand open on the moss with a green bronze ring on a finger. Everything grown together into one solid piece, nothing loose or floating.

A crude medieval Norse lantern: a small square box of dark hand-forged iron straps with thin scraped horn panes and a pointed iron cap, a stub of tallow candle inside, hanging on a short rusty chain from the end of a thick crooked grey wooden stake that leans out of a clump of brown reeds and green moss. The candle is not lit. Everything grown together into one solid piece, nothing loose or floating.

A tiny half-sunken Norse peat cutter's hut: thick walls of stacked dark brown peat blocks, a low roof of grass-grown turf, a small low wooden door on the front, a short chimney of flat stones, a stack of drying peat bricks and a long peat spade leaning beside the door. Everything grown together into one solid piece, nothing loose or floating.

A Norse charcoal kiln: a wide round dome-shaped mound of earth and turf built over stacked logs, a few small square vent holes around its base, a ring of black ash and lumps of black charcoal raked around it, a long wooden rake leaning against the mound. No fire, no smoke. Everything grown together into one solid piece, nothing loose or floating.

A massive ancient oak trunk, very thick and only about four metres tall, broken off at the top, its bark deeply furrowed and mossy, hollow at the base, with one thick stubby low branch sticking out sideways, and from that branch hangs a big green-bronze bell as large as a barrel on a short thick rusty chain, old ribbons and little carved wooden offerings tied around the trunk, moss and roots at its foot. Everything grown together into one solid piece, nothing loose or floating.

A huge troll's head turned to grey stone, the size of a barrel, lying on its side: a big crooked nose, heavy brow, a wide grinning mouth with blunt teeth, small closed eyes, stubby ears, rough lichen-spotted granite surface, cracks running through it. Everything grown together into one solid piece, nothing loose or floating.

Only the very top of an old Norse wooden bell tower sticking out of flat black bog mud and leaning badly: a small open belfry under a steep dark shingled pyramid roof with a carved dragon head at one corner, a dark bronze bell visible inside; the mud comes right up to the bottom of the belfry, no walls, no doors, no lower roofs, no cross; moss and reeds around where it sinks in, the timbers grey and rotting. Everything grown together into one solid piece, nothing loose or floating.

A pure white stag standing still on a mossy forest rock, head raised and turned, huge pale antlers like bare winter branches, its coat snow white and soft-looking, slender legs, standing on a low flat mossy stone base. Matte, softly lit, no glow. Everything grown together into one solid piece, nothing loose or floating.

The back of a huge sleeping lindorm, a Norse serpent dragon, rising out of black bog mud in three great scaly coils like a row of low arches, dark green-black scales with a pale ridge of spines along its spine, moss and reeds growing on the coils, no head visible, the ends of the coils sinking into the mud. Everything grown together into one solid piece, nothing loose or floating.
